settings.heading: Doing everything right, and still not feeling it
settings.body:
You train when you can, you eat well most of the time and you get to bed at a sensible hour, and yet by the middle of the afternoon you still feel as though you’re running on empty.

It tends to show up as an afternoon crash, a bit of brain fog and slower thinking at exactly the moment you need to be 100% there.

It shows up in your body too, as heavy legs on the stairs the morning after a session you would once have shaken off without noticing.

You’ve probably tried the obvious things already and found that nothing had a lasting impact, and that another coffee was more of a Band-Aid than a fix.

Meanwhile life doesn’t stop for any of it, because there is still work, children and travel to manage, and you can’t simply lie on the sofa until you feel better.

According to researchers, at least part of the explanation may be somewhere a little less obvious than your diary:
settings.key: The mitochondria in your cells make less energy as you get older.

settings.image_alt: A man in his fifties tying his trainers before a run

settings.body:
Mitochondria are the parts of your cells that turn the food you eat into ATP, which is the fuel that every cell in your body runs on.

When researchers compared the muscles of adults in their late 30s with those of adults in their late 60s, they found that the older group’s capacity to make energy was roughly half that of the younger group.

That may be part of the reason your body takes longer to bounce back than it used to, and why you can’t simply go again the next day in the way you once could.

settings.title: Muscle’s capacity to make energy, by age
settings.source: Conley KE, Jubrias SA, Esselman PC. Oxidative capacity and ageing in human muscle. J Physiol. 2000. Oxidative capacity per volume of muscle, shown relative to the younger group.

settings.label: Why it happens
settings.heading: Why energy falls with age
settings.text: Your cells run on ATP, which is made inside the mitochondria, and there are three changes that come with age which affect how much of it they are able to produce.
settings.step_1_text: Between your late 30s and your late 60s, the capacity of your muscles to make energy falls by roughly half.
settings.step_2_text: Your mitochondria depend on both of these molecules to do their work, and the levels of both fall with age in human tissue.
settings.step_3_text: Your stomach makes less acid as you get older, which makes vitamin B12 from food harder to absorb, and your skin makes less vitamin D from the same amount of sunlight.
settings.end: Caffeine doesn’t reverse any of this, because all it does is block the signal that tells your brain you’re tired, which is why the crash comes back as soon as it wears off.
settings.refs:

Short KR, et al. Decline in skeletal muscle mitochondrial function with aging in humans. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA. 2005.

settings.heading: 7 nutrients your cells rely on for energy
settings.body:
People often tell me they feel lost as to what really matters, so I would rather explain this properly than try to justify it.

These are the seven nutrients I look for as a cell biologist, with a plain-English account of what each one does, what the research says about it and where the evidence is still thin.

settings.title: NAD+
settings.dose: 300mg of nicotinamide riboside (NR), the maximum permitted in UK supplements
settings.body: NAD+ is found in every cell you have, and your mitochondria can’t turn food into energy without it, yet the amount in your tissues falls steadily as you get older. You can’t simply swallow NAD+ itself because it is poorly absorbed, so what you take instead is something your body can build it from, which is usually nicotinamide riboside (NR), a form of vitamin B3.
settings.science:
In samples of human skin, NAD+ levels were lower with age, from newborns to people in their 70s. | 1
In a placebo-controlled trial, 300mg of NR a day raised NAD+ in the blood by about 51% within two weeks. | 2
What we don’t know yet is whether raising NAD+ makes people feel more energetic. The trials so far have measured levels in the body.
settings.claim: Niacin (vitamin B3) contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism and to the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.
settings.refs:
Massudi H, et al. Age-associated changes in oxidative stress and NAD+ metabolism in human tissue. PLoS One. 2012.
Conze D, Brenner C, Kruger CL. Safety and metabolism of long-term administration of NIAGEN (nicotinamide riboside chloride) in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial of healthy overweight adults. Sci Rep. 2019.
Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, as retained in UK law: list of permitted health claims.

settings.title: CoQ10
settings.body: CoQ10 does one of the jobs in the chain of reactions that makes ATP inside your mitochondria, and although your body makes its own supply, it makes less of it after your twenties and you get very little from food.
settings.science:
CoQ10 levels in human organs, including the heart, are highest at around age 20 and then decline. | 1
A 2022 analysis of 13 randomised trials involving 1,126 people found that CoQ10 reduced fatigue scores compared with placebo. | 2
CoQ10 is fat-soluble and is absorbed better when taken with food. | 3
settings.refs:
Kalén A, Appelkvist EL, Dallner G. Age-related changes in the lipid compositions of rat and human tissues. Lipids. 1989.
Tsai IC, et al. Effectiveness of coenzyme Q10 supplementation for reducing fatigue: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Front Pharmacol. 2022.
Bhagavan HN, Chopra RK. Coenzyme Q10: absorption, tissue uptake, metabolism and pharmacokinetics. Free Radic Res. 2006.

settings.title: B vitamins, in their active forms
settings.dose: all eight B vitamins, with B12 as methylcobalamin, folate as 5-MTHF and B6 as P5P
settings.body: Nearly every step of getting energy out of your food needs a B vitamin, and because many products use forms that your body has to convert before it can use them, I look for the methylated versions, 5-MTHF and methylcobalamin, which don’t need that extra step.
settings.science:
Absorbing vitamin B12 from food becomes harder with age, mainly because the stomach makes less acid. | 1
A common variant of the MTHFR gene makes the enzyme that activates folic acid less efficient. | 2
5-MTHF raises folate levels at least as well as folic acid. | 3
settings.claim: Vitamins B2, B3, B5, B6, B12 and folate contribute to the reduction of tiredness and fatigue. Thiamin, riboflavin, niacin, pantothenic acid, vitamin B6, vitamin B12 and biotin contribute to normal energy-yielding metabolism.
settings.refs:
Baik HW, Russell RM. Vitamin B12 deficiency in the elderly. Annu Rev Nutr. 1999.
Frosst P, et al. A candidate genetic risk factor for vascular disease: a common mutation in methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase. Nat Genet. 1995.
Pietrzik K, Bailey L, Shane B. Folic acid and L-5-methyltetrahydrofolate: comparison of clinical pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Clin Pharmacokinet. 2010.
Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, as retained in UK law: list of permitted health claims.

settings.title: Creatine
settings.dose: 3 to 5g of creatine monohydrate a day
settings.body: People are often surprised to see creatine on this list because they think of it as something for the gym, but all it really does is help your muscles remake ATP quickly when you ask a lot of them, whether that is a set of squats or two flights of stairs.
settings.science:
The International Society of Sports Nutrition describes creatine monohydrate as the most effective supplement available for high-intensity exercise capacity. | 1
On a normal diet, creatine stores in muscle are around 60 to 80% full. | 1
Adults lose roughly 3 to 8% of their muscle mass each decade after 30. | 2
settings.claim: Creatine increases physical performance in successive bursts of short-term, high-intensity exercise. The beneficial effect is obtained with a daily intake of 3g of creatine.
settings.refs:
Kreider RB, et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation in exercise, sport, and medicine. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2017.
Volpi E, Nazemi R, Fujita S. Muscle tissue changes with aging. Curr Opin Clin Nutr Metab Care. 2004.
Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, as retained in UK law: list of permitted health claims.

settings.title: Zinc and copper, together
settings.dose: 15mg of zinc with 1mg of copper, both as bisglycinate
settings.body: Zinc helps your body process the carbohydrate, fat and protein you eat, and copper is part of one of the final enzymes in your mitochondria’s energy chain, but because the two compete with each other for absorption they are best taken together.
settings.science:
Zinc taken long-term without copper can lower the body’s copper levels. | 1
In a crossover study, zinc bisglycinate was absorbed 43% better than zinc gluconate. | 2
Zinc levels tend to fall with age. | 3
settings.claim: Copper contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism. Zinc contributes to normal macronutrient metabolism and to the protection of cells from oxidative stress.
settings.refs:
Fosmire GJ. Zinc toxicity. Am J Clin Nutr. 1990.
Gandia P, et al. A bioavailability study comparing two oral formulations containing zinc (Zn bis-glycinate vs. Zn gluconate) after a single administration to twelve healthy female volunteers. Int J Vitam Nutr Res. 2007.
Haase H, Rink L. The immune system and the impact of zinc during aging. Immun Ageing. 2009.
Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, as retained in UK law: list of permitted health claims.

settings.title: Vitamin D3 and K2
settings.dose: 2,000 IU of vitamin D3 with 100µg of vitamin K2 as MK-7
settings.body: Your muscles need vitamin D to work normally and your body makes it from sunlight, which is a problem in Britain between October and March and becomes more of one as you age, because older skin makes less of it anyway. Vitamin K2 is its usual partner.
settings.science:
Skin from people in their late 70s and 80s produced less than half the vitamin D of skin from young people. | 1
UK health advice is that everyone should consider a daily vitamin D supplement in autumn and winter. | 2
Vitamin D3 raises blood levels of vitamin D more effectively than D2. | 3
MK-7 stays in the body longer than vitamin K1. | 4
settings.claim: Vitamin D contributes to the maintenance of normal muscle function and normal bones. Vitamin K contributes to the maintenance of normal bones.
settings.refs:
MacLaughlin J, Holick MF. Aging decreases the capacity of human skin to produce vitamin D3. J Clin Invest. 1985.
Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition. Vitamin D and Health. 2016.
Tripkovic L, et al. Comparison of vitamin D2 and vitamin D3 supplementation in raising serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D status: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Am J Clin Nutr. 2012.
Schurgers LJ, et al. Vitamin K-containing dietary supplements: comparison of synthetic vitamin K1 and natto-derived menaquinone-7. Blood. 2007.
Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, as retained in UK law: list of permitted health claims.

settings.title: PQQ and trans-resveratrol
settings.body: I’ll be upfront and say that these two are the least proven nutrients on the list, because most of the research so far has been done in cells or in small groups of people, although both are being studied for what they do in the mitochondria.
settings.science:
In cell studies, PQQ activated a pathway that leads cells to build new mitochondria. | 1
In a small human study, PQQ changed markers in blood and urine linked to mitochondrial activity. | 2
Resveratrol has been widely studied in ageing research, including for its effect on cell pathways that depend on NAD+. | 3
settings.refs:
Chowanadisai W, et al. Pyrroloquinoline quinone stimulates mitochondrial biogenesis through cAMP response element-binding protein phosphorylation and increased PGC-1α expression. J Biol Chem. 2010.
Harris CB, et al. Dietary pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) alters indicators of inflammation and mitochondrial-related metabolism in human subjects. J Nutr Biochem. 2013.
Baur JA, Sinclair DA. Therapeutic potential of resveratrol: the in vivo evidence. Nat Rev Drug Discov. 2006.

It’s also worth saying that not everybody is a 25-year-old PT who can build their whole life around a routine.
